answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a stake that is slashed when an identity is proven to have double-voted or violated a signed rule. To gain influence, an attacker must fund many identities separately, lock capital in each, and risk losing it when disputes expose coordinated behavior; one cheap key cannot multiply voting power. This is no perfect defense—patient attackers can build reputation—but it turns a sybil tide from a fable into a costly campaign, with capital tied up until the summit of trust is reached.
